title: Android, Android TV, and Fire TV: Screen and controls
lead: Choose a source, edit separate source/player drafts and compare applied code, SDK state and events. This app also declares a TV launcher for Android TV and Android-based Fire TV; Vega OS is covered separately.

items.label: Implementation guide: PlayerConfig, source settings, UI customization and FAQ

blocks.text: Preparation and build

Build and launch apps/android using Android Studio or the documented command-line setup. Java 17 and required Android SDK packages are listed in Local setup and licenses and the implementation guide. The app uses Player 3.171.0. Allow com.playerlab.android on the Player license used by the build.

The same app declares a TV launcher for Android TV and Android-based Fire TV. Vega OS uses a separate app. The screenshots below were captured in a phone emulator; they do not establish remote-control reachability or playback on every TV or physical device.
Suggested screen workflow

Below the video are horizontal UI/source rows, live-seek buttons and a vertically scrollable form. Configuration edits basic source/player drafts; SDK API settings adds overrides; SDK API controls runs commands and reads state/events; Offline controls manages downloads. Scroll down to reach the panels.

items: Select VOD HLS or VOD DASH and start playback with the controls inside the player. Confirm that the picture and timeline advance before changing settings.
Open Configuration. Keep the current URL, enter Player Lab VOD for Title and choose Apply source (reload). Check the new source-load event and applied title without changing player settings.

For a player-settings comparison, set Startup threshold to 1, Restart threshold to 2 and Forward buffer to 10 seconds. Use Apply & restart player. Check the restart message, retained source and applied BufferConfig, then start playback if Autoplay is off.
Switch Default, Sports, Live (DVR) and Cinema to compare UI layouts. This replaces PlayerView while keeping the Player. Player-menu gestures and the surrounding form scroll independently.
Try audio, subtitles and bitrate settings with a source that provides suitable tracks or quality variants, following the examples below. A configured value does not add a missing track or rendition.

Open Show applied code and compare the applied settings. Then use SDK API controls → Commands, State and Events to connect an operation with its result. The following sections show these panels beside the relevant steps.

For live rewind, select a live preset and wait for an available window. The negative helper offsets are distances behind the live edge. Check mode, dvrAvailable, behindLive, window and the event log; Live edge returns to live.
If PlayerError or SourceError appears, check its numeric code. First check the application ID allowed by the license and connectivity to the reference source.

blocks.text: Changing UI replaces PlayerView while retaining the Player and source. Return to Default after comparison. The custom modes need the bundled shared JavaScript/CSS; if absent, follow the implementation guide to build and synchronize them. In the recorded SDK 3.171.0 phone-emulator check, foregrounding kept playback paused; press Play to resume when needed.

blocks.title: Checking TV devices
blocks.text: The Manifest declares LEANBACK_LAUNCHER for Android TV and Fire TV. Focus navigation, button reachability, remote controls, and actual playback still need testing on each device. A successful phone-emulator test does not establish behavior on physical devices or TVs.
Configuration drafts and applying changes

Source and Player have separate drafts. Applying player settings reloads the current applied source, not any source edits that have not been applied. Read the action label before submitting and correct highlighted validation errors.

Open Configuration to edit source and player settings. Source fields are a custom HTTP/HTTPS URL, DASH/HLS/Smooth/Progressive type, optional title, optional poster URL, persistent poster, start offset in seconds, SDK-default/Start/End reference, and optional live target latency in seconds. Blank title, poster, and offset use SDK defaults. The default reference is the start for VOD and the end for live streams; the SDK corrects offsets outside stream boundaries. HTTP depends on the device network policy.

blocks.caption: Android source settings: the source language list overrides the player list. An external WebVTT track has a URL, label, language and default metadata; enable it separately in the player subtitle menu. Android 16 emulator.

blocks.text: Live target latency maps to SourceLiveConfig.targetLatency. Blank keeps the original SDK defaults (liveConfig = null). An explicit finite value changes the SDK’s definition of the live edge and asks it to approach that latency while avoiding stalls; VOD ignores it. Apply source reloads the source, player recreation retains the applied value, and Reset source draft restores it without applying. This setting alone does not guarantee a seek-completion or latency-convergence deadline; the test results describe the checked environments.

Player fields are Autoplay (off), Start muted (off), SDK live time shifting (on), startup threshold (2.5 s), restart threshold (5 s), forward buffer (50 s), maximum automatic video bitrate (whole bps; blank means Int.MAX_VALUE / 2147483647, no ABR cap), preload (on), rebuffering (on), and live quality/stability balance (0–1; default 0.5). Thresholds must be nonnegative and at most forward buffer minus 0.5 s; forward buffer must be at least 0.5 s. Numeric fields reject non-finite values. The bitrate cap affects automatic selection; higher qualities remain available for manual selection. Balance applies near the live edge only.

blocks.caption: Android player settings: autoplay, mute and player-wide audio language priority. Applying these settings recreates the player; the source-specific audio list still takes precedence.

items: Edit a draft, then choose Apply source (reload) to load it in the existing player. Invalid drafts leave the applied source and player unchanged.

Choose Apply & restart player for playback, buffer, or adaptation changes. It creates a new player with the current source and its metadata/options, keeping UI mode, Allow DVR, and the event log. Playback position resets according to the source start offset and autoplay settings.

Reset source draft returns to the applied source. Reset player draft restores SDK defaults. Neither button applies changes. Selecting any catalog preset, including the same one again, replaces the source draft and clears custom metadata, offsets, and live target latency.

blocks.text: Scroll the panel vertically to reach all fields. Existing source, UI, and seek rows still scroll horizontally; new editor choices and actions wrap on narrow screens. Controls stay within safe system-bar and cutout insets. Use directional keys to move focus; focused configuration switches show an outline.

Show applied code displays Kotlin PlayerConfig, SourceConfig and PlayerViewConfig for the applied settings and current UI, including optional live target latency. Draft edits are excluded. Copy code writes the text to the Android clipboard and shows Copied; license keys use placeholders. The example still needs the integrating app’s keys, view attachment and lifecycle forwarding.

blocks.title: Scrolling menus inside the Android player
blocks.text: The player menu and the surrounding settings form are separate scroll areas. Swipe inside the video menu to reach lower items; start a swipe outside the video to scroll the form. A parent scroll view can intercept a gesture intended for the embedded menu, so the app keeps player touches with the video until they end or are cancelled. Replacing the player also releases that touch ownership.

rows: Start offset: 5 seconds; Offset reference: Start
Apply source (reload). On VOD, compare the first playback position with the beginning. Blank offset uses the SDK default. A retained offset also applies after a later player restart.
Apply & restart player. Check that playback waits for Play and starts muted. These are startup settings, separate from immediate controls in the player UI.
Startup threshold: 1; Restart threshold: 2; Forward buffer: 10, all in seconds

Apply & restart player. Startup/restart thresholds describe required buffered media before starting or resuming after a stall, not promised wall-clock delays. Inspect BufferConfig in applied code; the current network and source determine the visible effect.

Apply & restart player. Inspect maxSelectableVideoBitrate in applied code and compare automatic quality on a multi-bitrate source. This caps automatic selection; higher qualities remain available for manual selection.

Apply & restart player. Values toward 1 favor stability and values toward 0 favor quality near the live edge. VOD is unsuitable for comparing this setting. Preload content and Allow rebuffering are separate adaptation switches.
Player: en, de; Source: de, en

Apply the player list with restart, then the source list with reload. On a source containing those languages, check the selected audio in the player menu. The source list takes precedence; clear it to inherit the player list.
Apply & restart player. Check the normalized retry list in applied code. A successful playback request cannot demonstrate retries; use a test source you control when investigating failure handling.

blocks.text: To restore the original player settings, use Reset player draft and then Apply & restart player. Reset player draft alone does not change playback. Reset source draft instead restores the applied source values, not the catalog defaults. Select a source preset to clear custom source settings, including external subtitle metadata; player settings remain. Reapplying valid unchanged values still repeats the corresponding reload or restart on Android.

items: After Apply, open Show applied code and compare PlayerConfig, SourceConfig and the current UI configuration. Copy code writes the text to the Android clipboard and changes the button to Copied.

Edit a draft without applying and check that the output stays unchanged. Actual license values are placeholders. Additional SDK overrides are displayed separately under SDK API settings → Applied SDK override code.

blocks.caption: HTTP retry delays and applied Kotlin code. The displayed code uses the applied values and YOUR_PLAYER_KEY; draft-only edits and the actual license are excluded. Select the image to read it at full size.

blocks.title: Reset is not Apply
blocks.text: Reset source draft restores the applied source. Reset player draft stages player defaults; Apply & restart player is still required. Separately applied SDK overrides remain until removed in SDK API settings. Android basic forms repeat their reload/restart when valid unchanged values are applied again.
Audio language, external subtitles and retries

Player audio language priority sets an ordered list such as de, en when the player is created. Source audio language priority overrides it for that source when nonempty; blank inherits the player list. Codes keep their priority after trimming and removing duplicates without regard to case. No match leaves the SDK default track.

WebVTT is a text-based subtitle format with timed cues. To add one external track, enter its HTTP or HTTPS WebVTT URL and optionally a label and language code such as en-US. Default external subtitle sets isDefault metadata; it does not enable the subtitles. Apply source, then select the track in the Default UI settings menu. Clearing the URL also requires clearing its metadata. Existing in-stream subtitles remain available.

HTTP retry delays (s) controls the wait before each retry. Blank uses the SDK policy that increases the wait between retries, none disables retries, and a comma-separated list such as 0, 0.25, 2 permits one retry for each finite nonnegative value. The setting applies after player recreation. This standard field does not edit callbacks, request credentials or content-protection license renewal retries; use the separate SDK settings for their supported inputs.

Source changes reload the current player; player language and retry changes recreate it. Both paths keep the applied source metadata, selected UI and app rewind preference. Reset changes the draft only. Show applied code contains the same normalized settings and excludes unapplied text and actual license values.

items: To compare audio priority, apply Player en, de with restart, then Source de, en with reload. Read the selected audio in the player menu. Clear the source list and reload to inherit the player list.
To remove the external subtitle, clear its URL and metadata together and Apply source, or select a catalog preset. The Default external subtitle flag is metadata and does not enable captions.

To restore the normal HTTP retry policy, clear HTTP retry delays and Apply & restart player. A successful request cannot demonstrate retry timing; compare failed requests only on a source you control.

blocks.text: Additional SDK settings

items: Open SDK API settings and use Find SDK field to select a property. Read its type, accepted values and units.

Enter the value and choose Use this override to stage it. Check Staged overrides, then Apply SDK settings and restart. Staging alone does not affect playback; an applied override takes precedence over the basic form.

Inspect Applied SDK override code and refresh the matching State. Remove this override followed by Apply restores the basic form or SDK default. Reset SDK draft discards staged edits and restores the applied overrides; it does not remove an active override.

For a callback such as LabelingConfig.videoQualityLabeler, read input and the required result, stage a body and Apply. Trigger the matching SDK path, then Refresh callback outcomes to read calls, fallback and the last fallback reason.

rows: Add items and edit their child fields. Stage the entire list. Subtitle default metadata does not enable captions; playlist preloading may increase network and memory use.
Companion ad container, SimpleCache or Cronet engine
These controls create real Android objects. Prepare the Google Play services Cronet provider before applying Cronet. The cache tweak reads existing cached media; ordinary playback does not fill it.
Enter a JavaScript function body using input. The field explains the return type. Stage and Apply before it runs. Inspect callback counts and fallback results afterward.
Save the setting, fully stop the app and reopen it. The current process value and saved next-launch value are shown separately. Debug logs can contain confidential information; keep them local.

blocks.caption: An applied video-quality label callback. The staged body and active override are visible; the disabled Apply button indicates no pending change.

blocks.title: Callback execution
blocks.text: Callbacks use bounded plain values without Java/Android/Player object access. Invalid results or execution limits use the documented fallback. A zero call count means the SDK has not invoked that path. Read the implementation guide for language support, detailed limits and code reuse.
SDK operations, state and events

SDK API controls separates Commands, State and Events. A command can submit asynchronous work; its status message is separate from the actual playback effect. Keep a VOD source loaded for this seek comparison.

items: Open Commands, search Player.seek, enter 5 for time and Run SDK API. Read any argument or source-state error.

blocks.caption: Submitting a seek with an editable time argument.

items: Choose State, search Player.currentTime and Refresh SDK state. Read the value after seek completion; during playback it continues advancing. Refresh again after another command.

blocks.caption: Reading Player.currentTime after the seek. This is SDK state, separate from the command-submission message.

items: Choose Events and enable Record SDK events. Clear event counts before the next trial, perform Play/Pause or a supported seek, and inspect occurrence counts and latest SDK timestamps.

Zero means no occurrence has been recorded. PlayerView UI events use a separate prefix; playback belongs to Player and source events to Source. Clear event counts clears the history, not SDK playback state.

blocks.caption: Recorded Playing events. Events with no occurrence remain at zero.

blocks.text: View commands install fullscreen, Picture-in-Picture and custom Web UI message handlers. Check availability before entering PiP, then inspect its actual view state. Fullscreen returns with Back without discarding editor drafts. Use the matching exit/disable action when finishing a host-feature comparison.

MediaSession connects the current player to Android media controls. Enable the native MediaSession command, inspect the controls, then disable/release it when finished. External-device behavior depends on the host system.

blocks.caption: The native MediaSession command. Enabling it connects the current player to Android media controls; external-device behavior depends on the host system.

blocks.text: Cast, advertising, encrypted media and VR need matching content, a receiver/device or a connected service. Read availability and active state rather than the submission message alone. The VR renderer uses a real decoding surface and requires a compatible source VR content type; disable the renderer to restore normal PlayerView presentation.

Analytics controls edits collection and metadata separately. Apply Analytics settings and restart player applies its draft; Reset Analytics draft discards unapplied edits. Perform a known playback and inspect collected sessions in Bitmovin Dashboard. A local SDK result does not prove backend receipt; the implementation guide explains Analytics/Observability after player integration.
Offline downloads and playback

items: Open Offline controls. Choose Use sample DASH source or apply a downloadable on-demand source. Set Stable content ID, then Create manager for current source. Keep the ID to address the same asset again.
Choose simultaneous download/segment limits, device/network requirements and offline DRM handling, then Apply offline configuration. Downloads can wait until all selected requirements hold.

Fetch SDK options. Set each required track to Download, Delete or None, then Process selected actions. Nothing is selected automatically; the SDK can reject an action that does not match the track state.

blocks.caption: Selecting an audio track for download. This figure shows the selection step, before completion is established.

items: Inspect Progress and Read offline SDK state, then wait for the manager’s completed state. Only then use Play downloaded source and compare video/audio with networking disabled. Track selection or submission is not completion.

Suspend/Resume controls work in progress. Delete all content for this ID removes its cached content; Release manager keeps the files while releasing the manager. Select a catalog preset to return to a remote source.

blocks.text: Offline DRM needs suitable rights, a license service and storage. License download/renew/release is separate from media-download completion. Advanced offline source constructor does not import an SDK-managed download or issue a license. For ordinary managed downloads use Play downloaded source so the SDK supplies matching cache/track metadata.
